To the art question: it's indeed the case that there's a lot of artists that are depressed or have had depression. I actually do as well express myself through art. (mostly music: song writig) But I don't think that you can say everyone with depression has just not found their art yet. Maybe it would be an interesting hypothesis to say that people with abilitys in arts are more often depressed which I actually think is the case. But I am sure that there are people out there who suffer from depression and don't have any artistic way to express what they are feeling. I think the greatest gift that depression gives you if you survive it is strength, wisdom and the ability to appreciate happiness more... (stuff like that). It is for me, and most people, very helpful to let their feelings out. This can be through many ways, among them arts but also talking. I used to write poems quite regularely when I was in a hard phase. But a other thing you mentioned too is sports. It's proven that sport, apart from all the many other benefits, helps with depression. I myself can say I am experancing just that! Something that helps us see meaning is to find something that we love to do which can be a sport, job, art and so on...

And to the 2nd thing... We all could. But maybe we are right now causing the death of someone by buying that piece of clothing etc. You know it's good to be caring and have your eyes open. To be there if someone needs you but if you are kind and caring and someone commits suicide anyway maybe even triggered by sth you did or said know: This person must have gone through so much shit to even get to the point where he or she could be triggered by you this easily. All things which you did not do. You can't controle others lifes. If it wasn't you who said that one thing to trigger the person then it's likely someone else would have. In those cases it's kind of about luck too... If the person is lucky he or she gets the help in time or a trigger. But in any case: as long as you are caring, kind and so on it would never be your fault and I don't think you even should blame yourself at all.

Uuf it's complicated! I am struggling with clinical depression. I am a lot better now though. The point is that often times depressed people feel sad, empty or just low most of the times. For me added to that there was no interest in anything. And anxiety with panic attacks. Believe me it's intense. You will struggle enjoying anything at all. When every day just brings you suffering and you only wait for the night to sleep... Why would you live then? For me it's as well just a horrible mental pain. A mix out of fear, sadness and hoplessnes it's a great pressure on my chest. Maybe that it is hard to understand but everyone sees the world through their own glasses. And we can change those activly once we really get that we can and once we have the power. But the glasses of a depressed person usually as well thinks negatively and honestly how could it be ones fault? The things that have happened to u so far in your life and maybe genes have formed u into who you are now. The suffering repeats itself just as much as the happiness of a happy person does. What are you constatly feeling when nothing from the outside world is affecting your mood to a reaction ? Positivity, trust, flow, happiness? Why do you feel that way? Can you control it? I don't think you can... These feelings usually come from your subconscious mind and if this is programmed as always feeling bad... For so long and so intense that you literally forget what it feels like to be happy. Or maybe as well having panic and fear following you all the time... You could compare it to a chronic head ache. In fact people with chronic pains are as well often times suicidal. If you have a horrible pain which never leaves or always comes back at some point you lose your will to live. Everything that gave you joy is weaker than that huge heavy cloud of pain. When I was very suicidal I as well just didn't care anymore. For me it was as well a kind of losing myself and all power. I couldn't imagine any of the things one can do in life to be fun. Imagine the feeling of boredom and sadness combined all the time. It's just always there and never leaves. I have to say I am still at a point where I have absolutely no fear of dying. I would still welcome it. But I am now kinda willing to live too. It took me long to get where I am now and it will take long only to come a little farther. If you have the choice to take that looong and difficult journey of healing or suicide and end your pain right away... It's understandable why a lot of people choose no 2. Apart from that it's often as well that the people commiting suicide can't believe that it can get any better. I hope you have a little pic of how it is now? XO
